title: Terraform IAM binding standardizer and least-privilege policy catalog for Private deploys
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Goal: Deliver a reusable Terraform module and companion pipelines that standardize IAM bindings and ship a curated least-privilege policy catalog for Private (VPC) deployments. This ticket covers schema, module boundaries, upgrade safety, policy linter integration, and automated healthchecks to detect drift or over-privileged bindings.

Scope:
- Terraform module: `redwood_priv_iam_catalog` that provides canonical role definitions, binding templates, and an opinionated API for tenant-scoped and infra-scoped permissions.
- Policy catalog: JSON/YAML canonical policies with semantic versioning (vMajor.Minor) and change notes.
- Safety and upgrade path: diffs + canary apply pattern, automated preflight checks, and rollback hooks.
- CI: policy lint (checkov/tfsec rules), unit tests for module (terratest), and PR gate that rejects policy additions without justification.
- Drift detection: periodic healthcheck that scans Terraform state and cloud IAM bindings and emits alerts and remediation playbooks.

Out of scope:
- RBAC UI surface in Console (separate PM ticket).
- Fine-grained tenant-specific exceptions (handled in downstream wiring tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Module publishes a stable Terraform registry package with inputs for 'role_catalog_version', 'binding_templates', and 'trust_boundaries'
CI blocks merges if policy lint or terratest fails
Canary upgrade flow documented and automated: canary subset (one project) -> measure healthchecks -> full rollout or automated rollback
Healthcheck runs weekly and flags mismatches between catalog and live bindings; alert to #infra-sec and creates a task if drift > 2 bindings
Security review sign-off recorded in ticket and release notes include policy diff summary
implementation_notes: Module design: split into three submodules (catalog, bindings, audit-hook) but expose single composable module for consumers
Use semantic version tags for policies, store canonical policies in git under /policies/priv/ with changelog.md per policy
Terraform schema: accept map(string) for binding templates; use for_each to generate aws_iam_policy and aws_iam_role_policy_attachment (or GCP equivalents) depending on target provider variable
Upgrade safety: implement `policy_version_locked` boolean on consumers and a 'preview_plan' job that computes a diff and posts to PR as artifact
CI: implement GitHub Action that runs tflint + checkov + terratest (Go) leveraging lightweight emulators where possible
Healthcheck: implement lambda/k8s-cron that compares catalog -> live; store last_scan_result in datastore and emit structured events to Opsgenie and Slack
Fallback: if canary healthcheck fails, trigger terraform apply to re-apply previous policy_version (rollback) via a locked-state job
Auditing: emit audit log entries for policy changes to the customer audit log (for Private installs, wire to customer KMS/HSM per infra docs)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect least-privilege assumptions could break customer infra — Mitigation: require 'owner justification' field on any increase in privileges and run sandboxed integration tests
Risk: Terraform provider differences between AWS/GCP/Azure — Mitigation: provider abstraction layer and integration tests per cloud provider
Risk: Drift detection noise causing pager fatigue — Mitigation: thresholding, grouping similar diffs into single alert, and a human review step before auto-remediation
Risk: Policy rollout introduces transient authorization errors — Mitigation: staged canary + automated rollback + clear runbook for on-call
